Rationale: per-subcarrier CSI up to 80 MHz (up to 4x4 on RT-AC86U) via Nexmon firmware patch; delivered as UDP/pcap. REPRODUCIBLE TODAY (with pinning discipline) -- the strongest firmware-patched commodity CSI story in the catalog because the maintainers ported it forward. Supports Raspberry Pi 3B+/4B/5; a Makefile.rpi now targets recent Pi OS kernels (4.19/5.4/5.10) with no modified brcmfmac driver. Pitfalls: BCM43455c0 firmware is PINNED to microcode string 7_45_189 (must match your shipped brcmfmac43455-sdio.bin), and 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS (Bookworm) has toolchain/firmware-path friction -- many use the 32-bit image or the nexmonster/zeroby0 one-liner fork. 171 open issues, dominated by data-quality (amplitude scaling, dropped/null subcarriers), not build failures. See ../docs/verification-tier2-csi.md, ../chips/broadcom-cypress.md and ../projects/nexmon.md.

key_projects.name: BCM43684 AP CSI for IoT forensics (arXiv 2305.10554)

notes: CORRECTION to prior catalog tier-0 entry: AX-CSI demonstrably extracts full HE-PHY CSI from the BCM43684 (Asus RT-AX86U) up to 160 MHz, 4x4 MIMO, up to 32768 complex subcarriers per frame (2048/stream), delivered as crafted UDP datagrams. Nexmon lineage: D11 core patched to freeze the radio on a target frame, Wi-Fi OS (ARM) patched to read the four per-core PHY tables (<=8192 values each; stream k at offset k*2048; 160 MHz VHT split across [0,256) and [1024,1280)). This raises the part from black-box tier 0 to tier 2 (CSI), openness patchable. Tool released on request via axcsi@unibs.it; no public repo. This is the REAL 'AX-CSI' -- it is a Broadcom tool, NOT an Intel one, contrary to sibling files chips/intel.md and projects/csi-toolchains.md which mis-attribute AX-CSI to Intel AX200/AX210. The Intel AX2xx HE-CSI path is PicoScenes/FeitCSI (intel-ax200-ax201, intel-ax210-ax211, intel-ax210-csi).

Integrated Wi-Fi 6 gateway SoC bundling an application CPU with an on-die AX radio. Closed, no port → tier 0.

notes: Wi-Fi 6/6E access-point SoC on Broadcom's closed router SDK. No Nexmon foothold and no open driver; effectively black-box for SDR-style repurposing. Listed for completeness alongside BCM4398; for an open 6E AP for sensing, prefer an MT7916-class MediaTek AP instead.

firmware.arch: Broadcom D11 MAC microcontroller (custom ISA; MAC ucode uploaded by host at bring-up)

notes: The archetypal open-firmware Wi-Fi platform: the MAC ucode is GPL source you assemble with b43-asm and upload via the b43 driver, replacing Broadcom's proprietary ucode. tier_5 reflects FIRMWARE openness only. The PHY is a closed hardware block configured by opaque initvals; RF flexibility is minimal. 802.11b/g (2.4 GHz) only, no 802.11n+, no CSI, no raw IQ, no arbitrary waveform. Enables custom MAC timing, TDMA MACs, ACK-policy changes, and MAC-timing covert channels. Match the generated ucode revision (e.g. ucode5.fw) to the card's D11 core revision. Some BCM4306 A-PHY variants may add 5GHz but OpenFWWF targets G-PHY parts.

Earlier Celeno 802.11ac (Wave 2) AP silicon, before the Wi-Fi Doppler Imaging engine that defines the catalogued CL2x4x/CL6000 'Denali' parts. Fully closed with no public driver or RE tooling — Tier 0. Catalogued to close out the Celeno line; the sensing story lives on celeno-cl6000. Net-new record.

firmware.arch: vendor RTOS on internal MAC/PHY processor

notes: Purpose-built Wi-Fi 6 AP SoC marketed by Celeno (acquired by Renesas in 2022) with an on-chip 'Wi-Fi Doppler Imaging' sensing mode doing Doppler/CSI-based motion, people counting/localization, and presence-for-HVAC. Notable as a chip DESIGNED as a sensor and a natural 802.11bf home, but firmware is fully closed and the sensing observables are not user-accessible, so it is Tier 0 for SDR/DIY repurposing. Included as the 'chip basis' behind productized presence/occupancy sensing, not as a repurposable SDR. No public firmware RE tooling exists.

Built-in Wi-Fi Doppler radar mode (WFD) detects presence, falls, gestures, even breathing through walls in 5/6 GHz. The purest Wi-Fi-as-radar product in the catalog, but the Doppler engine is a closed proprietary feature with no public API, firmware, or RE tooling: tier 2 by capability but locked.
BLE 5 Cortex-M0 SoC from an ADC/MCU vendor branching into wireless. Closed SDK. Tier 0.

Cisco's own proprietary 802.11b radio/MAC (not Atheros, not Prism), driven by the in-tree airo module which supports monitor mode but not injection. On-card firmware is an opaque flashable blob. Distinct from the AR5212-based CB21AG.

Integrator: the CB21AG/PI21AG is an Atheros AR5212 a/b/g die behind Cisco branding. Full RFMON monitor + frame injection under ath5k/MadWifi. Score by the AR5212 die — cross-reference chips/qualcomm-atheros.md. Do not confuse with the proprietary Aironet 340/350 (cisco-aironet-350).
Ultra-low-power 1x1 combo aimed at wearables/IoT. Cypress/Infineon SDK gives partial documentation; no confirmed Nexmon monitor/CSI. Candidate for future porting.
Single-stream 11n IoT part running Cypress WICED SoftAP firmware (e.g. Particle Photon). Closed FullMAC, no monitor/port → tier 0. RE potential noted but unexplored.

1x1 11n combo (rebranded BCM4343W) found across countless embedded/IoT boards. brcmfmac-driven FullMAC with no mac80211 monitor and no Nexmon port → tier 0. Ubiquity makes it a high-value future target.
1x1 11ac USB combo driven by brcmfmac. Same D11+ARM family; monitor/injection plausible via a Nexmon port but unproven. Attractive because USB-attached and cheap.
AIROC 2x2 Wi-Fi 5 (11ac) + Bluetooth combo. Closed FullMAC firmware, no public RE or port → tier 0.
Automotive-grade 2x2 11ac with 802.11p (DSRC/V2X). Same lineage; no public RE. Cataloged for future 802.11p-repurposing interest.

Integrator/rebadge family — tier depends entirely on the die of the specific revision: DWL-650=Prism2, DWL-520=Prism2.5, DWL-G650=Atheros AR5212 (ath5k), DWL-G122 revisions=Ralink RT2570 / Prism GT / Marvell. Score by die; cross-reference chips/qualcomm-atheros.md, chips/mediatek-ralink.md and the Prism2 family.

common_hardware: Doodle Labs Mesh Rider embedded/mini-PCIe radios
notes: Integrator: OpenWrt on Qualcomm Atheros silicon (IPQ40xx SoCs with QCA9880/9882/9888 or AR9xxx radios), in sub-GHz/2.4/5GHz variants. Inherits the full Atheros ladder — ath9k monitor+injection+CSI (Tier 2) and ath10k spectral scan (Tier 3) on QCA988x. Tier belongs to the die; cross-reference chips/qualcomm-atheros.md and projects/csi-toolchains.md.

family: Sub-GHz/2.4 GHz carrier modules over Semtech/TI/SiLabs die
notes: Carrier boards (Ebyte E-series, NiceRF/G-NiceRF) for every chip on this page plus PA/LNA front ends. Two use modes: (a) transparent-UART firmware, convenient but opaque, effectively an RN2483-style closed box; (b) strip firmware and talk SPI to the bare Semtech/TI/SiLabs die, restoring the host chip's full Tier-1 register control. Real capability = the inner chip; the module part number identifies it. Warning: H/PA variants emit +20..+30 dBm (regulatory/PA-damage risk without proper antenna/attenuator).

Package around Espressif's own ESP8266 SoC (not a foreign die). Documented SDK gives promiscuous/monitor RX and raw frame TX (esp_wifi_80211_tx) → Tier 1; no first-party CSI on ESP8266. See ../chips/espressif.md.

The reference CSI platform: built-in esp_wifi_set_csi_config/esp_wifi_set_csi_rx_cb yields per-subcarrier complex CSI (up to 52-64 usable subcarriers HT20). Raw TX via esp_wifi_80211_tx, promiscuous RX with rx_ctrl (RSSI/noise/rate/timestamp). No FFT/spectral or IQ API -> hard tier-2 ceiling. Wi-Fi MAC/PHY shipped as closed libpp/libnet80211/libphy blobs.

Cost-optimized, thin RAM/flash. Monitor + raw TX verified. CSI is limited/unverified: the C2 is notably absent from Espressif's canonical CSI-support enumeration (ESP32/S2/C3/S3/C5/C6/C61). Treat CSI as reported at best on this SKU.
First RISC-V Espressif Wi-Fi part; cheapest reliable CSI node. Full CSI/monitor/raw-TX support. Open RV32 core toolchain, closed Wi-Fi PHY blob (same tier-2 ceiling).
Package around Espressif's RISC-V ESP32-C3 SoC. Same documented CSI/monitor/injection = Tier 2. Cross-reference ../chips/espressif.md and ../chips/risc-v-wifi.md.

Espressif's first dual-band (2.4/5 GHz) Wi-Fi 6 SoC, single RISC-V core. Exposes per-subcarrier CSI via the documented ESP-IDF CSI callback API (tier 2), and is explicitly listed among esp-csi's fully supported parts (ESP32/S2/C3/S3/C5/C6/C61). Wi-Fi/BT firmware is a closed blob but the CSI/RF-config API is documented. Recent silicon — use current ESP-IDF.

firmware.arch: 32-bit RISC-V HP core (160 MHz) + LP core; RV32IMAC

notes: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) + BLE 5 + 802.15.4 (Thread/Zigbee/Matter). CSI/monitor/TX supported. HE CSI has documented rough edges: IDF #14271 reports missing L-LTF data and wrong HT-LTF subcarrier ordering in the callback. HT (11n) CSI is solid; HE CSI is evolving.

Package around Espressif's RISC-V ESP32-C6 SoC — Wi-Fi 6 (2.4GHz) with first-party CSI = Tier 2, plus an 802.15.4 radio for Thread/Zigbee. Cross-reference ../chips/espressif.md and ../chips/risc-v-wifi.md.

Cost-reduced 2.4 GHz-only Wi-Fi 6 RISC-V SoC. Supports the same documented ESP-IDF CSI extraction path as the rest of the family (tier 2) and is listed in esp-csi's supported set. Very new (2024/2025); board and toolchain availability still maturing.

firmware.arch: Xtensa LX6/LX7 (ESP32/S-series) or RISC-V (C-series); Wi-Fi MAC closed blob, CSI via public API

notes: Rationale: native ESP-IDF wifi_csi_info_t exposes up to 52/64 subcarriers (L-LTF/HT-LTF), 1x1; no firmware reversing needed. MOST REPRODUCIBLE Tier-2 entry in the catalog and the reference point the others are measured against: it has NO host-kernel dependency (CSI runs on the MCU, host just reads serial/CSV), it is a documented vendor API, and esp-csi is actively maintained (200+ commits) advertising CSI across the whole current line (ESP32/S2/S3/C3/C5/C6/C61) -- git clone + idf.py build flash reproduces it on today's ESP-IDF. Caveat: ESP32-C6 802.11ax (HE-LTF) CSI has reported subcarrier-ordering/null quirks (esp-idf issues, e.g. #14271-class); the mature path is 11n HT-LTF CSI on the classic ESP32. See ../docs/verification-tier2-csi.md and ../chips/espressif.md.

NO Wi-Fi radio -> no Wi-Fi CSI, out of the core Wi-Fi-SDR thesis. Included for completeness: it offers raw 802.15.4 frame RX/TX at 2.4 GHz (a different-standard analog of monitor/injection) plus BLE 5. Catalogued at the floor for Wi-Fi purposes.

firmware.arch: RISC-V RV32IMAFC dual-core (HP) @400 MHz + LP core
re_tooling: ESP-IDF (fully documented HAL, no radio blob)

notes: Honest edge case: a high-performance dual-core RISC-V application processor with NO integrated radio. Wi-Fi/BLE come only from an external companion (ESP32-C5/C6) over SDIO/SPI via esp-hosted. Tier 0 for SDR purposes, and included as a family member + caution that 'RISC-V + Espressif' does not imply a radio. Ironically the most-open Espressif chip precisely because it has no Wi-Fi blob to hide.
Wi-Fi only (no Bluetooth). Full CSI/monitor/raw-TX API parity with ESP32. Native USB-OTG makes it a clean USB-tethered CSI capture dongle.

firmware.arch: Tensilica Xtensa LX7 (dual-core + vector/SIMD DSP, 240 MHz)

notes: Same CSI/monitor/TX APIs as ESP32; the LX7 vector extensions make on-device CSI feature extraction and TinyML sensing (motion/respiration classifiers) viable without offloading.
Package around Espressif's ESP32-S3 SoC. Same CSI/monitor/injection story as ESP32 (Tier 2) with more compute + vector instructions for on-device ML on the CSI stream. See ../chips/espressif.md.

Package around Espressif's own ESP32 SoC. First-party CSI API (ESP32-CSI-Tool) plus monitor + raw frame TX = Tier 2 — one of the cheapest documented CSI nodes available. ESP32-WROVER is the same die with added PSRAM. See ../chips/espressif.md.

firmware.arch: Xtensa LX6 (dual-core), closed Wi-Fi MAC/PHY blob driven via ESP-IDF esp_wifi APIs

notes: Documented CSI path via ESP-IDF: per-packet wifi_csi_info_t exposes complex channel estimates for the LLTF/HT-LTF subcarriers (64 subcarriers = 128 bytes for HT20, each subcarrier two int8_t as imaginary-then-real). Genuine Tier 2 CSI: usable for amplitude-based respiration/presence sensing after host-side DSP (subcarrier selection, 0.1-0.5 Hz bandpass, FFT). NOT SDR: no IQ, no arbitrary-waveform TX, no raw PHY; Wi-Fi MAC/PHY remains a closed blob and CSI is a demodulation byproduct. Raw phase is CFO/SFO-limited across two boards, so amplitude is the practical observable. Tier 2 ceiling on this chip.

Monitor + injection are the classic, verified use (deauth/sniffer platform). CSI is documented in Espressif's ESP-FAQ via esp_wifi_set_csi_rx_cb() but the mainstream CSI toolkits (ESP32-CSI-Tool, Wi-ESP) are all ESP32; ESP8266 CSI is reported, not community-proven. No spectral/IQ access. Wi-Fi PHY is a closed blob.

firmware.arch: AD936x/AD9371 transceiver + Spartan/Kintex/Zynq FPGA (open UHD, large FPGA on N310)

notes: Research-standard. B200/B210 70MHz-6GHz 56MHz BW 12-bit; N310 4x4 10MHz-6GHz up to 100MHz/ch 14-bit. Far end of the yardstick; instrument-grade open PHY.

firmware.arch: Xilinx Spartan-6 FPGA + Cypress FX3 firmware; UHD host driver

notes: Full-duplex 2x2 SDR, 70 MHz-6 GHz, up to 56 MHz bandwidth (AD9361), 12-bit, USB 3.0. Open FPGA source and UHD driver. The comfortable platform for real-time 20 MHz 802.11 in software. Genuine SDR, catalog Tier-5 baseline.

firmware.arch: Xilinx Spartan-3A DSP FPGA; UHD host driver over GbE

notes: Networked SDR with swappable RF daughterboards; ~25 MHz usable bandwidth over Gigabit Ethernet, 14-bit ADC. The original reference platform in the Bloessl et al. gr-ieee802-11 papers. Genuine SDR, catalog Tier-5 baseline.
Die = Realtek RTL8733BS-class (reported) 11n + BT5. Tier 1 via the Realtek driver monitor/injection path; no CSI. Cross-ref ../chips/realtek.md and ../chips/monitor-injection-support.md.
Die = Realtek RTL8822CS-class (reported) dual-band 11ac + BT5. Tier 1 (rtw88-family monitor/injection), no Nexmon-class CSI path. Cross-ref ../chips/realtek.md.

firmware.arch: STM32WB55 MCU driving CC1101 over SPI; open-source firmware Sub-GHz app (Read/Read RAW/Frequency Analyzer)

common_hardware: external CC1101 SubGHz add-on modules (SMA antenna)
notes: The most accessible sub-GHz capture/replay platform. Exposes CC1101 bands 300-348/387-464/779-928 MHz, default 433.92 MHz AM650. Captures decoded static protocols (Princeton, CAME, Nice FLO, Holtek) and raw OOK envelope timings to human-readable .sub files (RAW_Data microsecond edge lists). Deliberately does not run rolling-code attacks. Tier 1: no IQ, no CSI, fixed ISM front-end; external modules improve antenna/gain only, not capability class. Legal only against devices you own.

Carries the Realtek RTL8723BS die (11n 2.4G + BT). Realtek monitor/injection is driver-dependent (out-of-tree forks) → Tier 1. Capability from the die; see ../chips/realtek.md. Fn-Link also ships AP6212-style Broadcom variants — check the FCC ID.
Carries the Realtek RTL8822CS die (dual-band 11ac + BT5). Monitor/injection via rtw88/vendor driver → Tier 1. See ../chips/realtek.md.

re_tooling: Morse Micro GPL-2.0 mac80211 driver / OpenWrt SDK

notes: M.2 HaLow radio card built on Morse Micro MM8108 (second-gen). Targets embedded gateways/SBCs. Inherits Morse open GPL mac80211 driver (tier-1 monitor+injection) and closed MM8108 firmware blob + BCF. Net-new named module record; complements the earlier NRC7292-based Gateworks GW16146 mini-PCIe.

firmware.arch: Wi-Fi 6E SoC (chipset not publicly confirmed), Google firmware

notes: Wi-Fi 6E tri-band mesh AP listed among Android's RTT-capable (802.11mc responder) access points, with 6 GHz operation relevant to 802.11az next-gen positioning. Closed firmware, no researcher-facing SDR surface; catalogued only as an FTM responder (ranging primitive, tier 1, no capability flags). firmware.arch: Qualcomm IPQ4019 (ARM Cortex-A7), Google Wi-Fi firmware

notes: Consumer mesh AP built on Qualcomm IPQ4019; one of the canonical 802.11mc FTM responders Android's Wi-Fi RTT stack was validated against. Firmware is closed and exposes no monitor/CSI/raw path to a researcher — its only relevance to this catalog is as a cooperative FTM responder (a ranging primitive, hence tier 1 with no SDR capability flags). Not an initiator use case; you range TO it from a phone/laptop.
1MHz-6GHz, 20MHz BW, 8-bit, half-duplex TX/RX. Canonical open TX-capable hacker SDR; the arbitrary-waveform reference.

firmware.arch: HackRF One radio (MAX2837 + MAX5864, 1 MHz-6 GHz, 8-bit, half-duplex) + PortaPack LCD/MCU add-on running standalone firmware

notes: Add-on board (LCD, navigation, battery) that turns a HackRF One into a standalone, no-PC transceiver; the open-source Mayhem firmware supplies on-device TX/RX apps (replay, ADS-B/POCSAG/AIS/RDS generation, jammer, spectrum). Same 1 MHz-6 GHz / 8-bit / half-duplex HackRF radio underneath -- so genuine arbitrary-waveform TX (Tier 4), just field-portable. Add-on ~$100-250 on top of a HackRF host. Distinct from the bare HackRF (greatscott-hackrf-one) by its standalone firmware and form factor.

Open 2.4 GHz platform: CC2400 transceiver + LPC1756 Cortex-M3, fully open firmware (bluetooth_rxtx). Sniffs BLE, partial BT Classic (BR), and runs ubertooth-specan, a real spectrum-analyzer/spectral-scan across 2.4 GHz via CC2400 RSSI sweeps (tier 3). Because the firmware is yours, the CC2400's PHY telemetry is fully exposed.

Genuine wideband SDR, 1 MHz-6 GHz, ~20 Msps over USB 2.0, 8-bit, half-duplex. Fully open firmware. Cheapest platform for running gr-ieee802-11; 8-bit dynamic range and half-duplex limit performance vs USRP. Reference Tier-5 baseline for the catalog, not a repurposed Wi-Fi chip.

CC1111 = CC1101 radio + 8051 + USB. YARD Stick One runs RfCat (open firmware) exposing the transceiver from an interactive Python shell: 2-FSK/GFSK/MSK/ASK/OOK, raw register access, RSSI-sweep spectrum. RfCat also supports CC1110/CC2510/CC2511.
Huawei's first Wi-Fi 6 + BT 5.1 combo. Fully captive: no public SDK/datasheet, signed closed firmware, no known monitor/injection path. Tier 0.
Router/CPE-oriented Wi-Fi 6 sibling of Hi1103. Closed, captive. Tier 0.
Reported later HiSilicon Wi-Fi 6E/7-class combo with sparse public documentation; band/standard set is best-effort. Closed. Tier 0, listed for completeness.

Semtech SX1231/SX1231H GFSK/OOK engine (no LoRa) on a module. 315/433/868/915 MHz, direct mode supported. Cheap, well-supported (RadioHead, LowPowerLab, RadioLib RF69 class) OOK/FSK front end for CTC and replay experiments. HW variant adds +20 dBm PA. Tier 1.

Repackaged Semtech SX1276/77/78 die on a castellated module (RFM95 868/915, RFM96 433, RFM98 lower bands). Inherits the full semtech-sx127x repurposing story: LoRa + FSK/OOK packets and the transmitDirect/receiveDirect DIO1-clk/DIO2-data raw-bitstream mode (FSK only). Tier 1. See semtech-sx127x for the die-level detail.
AIROC ultra-low-power 1x1 Wi-Fi 5 + BLE combo (announced ~2023) aimed at wearables. Closed FullMAC, no public RE or port → tier 0. Firmware openness unknown.

common_hardware: Raspberry Pi Pico W / Pico 2 W
notes: 1x1 802.11n combo, the Wi-Fi in the Raspberry Pi Pico W. Genuinely Nexmon-supported: the table lists bcm43439a0 with firmware 7_95_49 (Cypress build 2271bb6) for monitor+injection → tier 1, patchable. Cypress/Infineon rebrand of a 43438-class die but with a distinct part number and its own firmware line, so a net-new entry (not the catalogued broadcom-bcm43438).

120 GHz FMCW transceiver for short-range high-resolution industrial sensing. Raw-IQ radar with external digitization. Band listed as 60GHz enum bucket (>52 GHz); actual carrier ~120 GHz. Tier 4 radar.

24.0-24.25 GHz ISM (K-band) Doppler/CW radar front-end (1TX/1RX) with analog I/Q IF output you digitize with any external ADC. CW/Doppler primary; FMCW possible with an external ramp. Tier 3 (simple modulation, external ADC). CORRECTION (cycle-8 audit batch 2): bands was mis-tagged 2.4GHz — a 10x error; 24 GHz K-band has no enum bucket, so bands set to [] to match the sibling infineon-bgt24mtr11-radar and avoid falsely implying the 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi/BLE band. True frequency documented here and in standards.

key_projects.name: UWB CIR for device-free localization (MDPI Sensors)

notes: Ultra-wideband (~500 MHz channels, 3.5-6.5 GHz). The CIR accumulator exposes the full complex channel impulse response, up to 1016 taps of 16-bit I + 16-bit Q at ~1 ns spacing over SPI: a UWB analog of CSI with amplitude and phase. Basis for a large body of device-free localization, occupancy, and (monostatic) radar-style sensing. Tier 2 reaching toward tier 3; fully documented, no firmware to reverse. sdr_reason: 1x1 2.4GHz 11n SoftMAC; spectral scan (Tier 3) and single-stream CSI (Tier 2) both work through the open driver / CSI Tool.

firmware.arch: none — SoftMAC, driven by host ath9k driver

sdr_reason: 2x2 2.4GHz 11n SoftMAC; 2-stream CSI (Tier 2) plus spectral FFT (Tier 3). Also serves as the radio behind an AR7010 USB bridge.
notes: The 2.4GHz-only sibling of AR9280.

firmware.arch: ath9k SoftMAC (PHY logic in open driver, no separate blob)

notes: Rationale: uncompressed per-subcarrier CSI (56@20/114@40) via ath9k driver hook (Tier 2); same silicon dumps raw FFT bins via spectral_scan (Tier 3). REPRODUCIBILITY SPLIT (2025): the Tier-3-defining spectral_scan path is in MAINLINE ath9k debugfs and works on current kernels out of the box -- it ages better than the CSI rung beneath it. The Atheros-CSI-Tool CSI path is VERIFIED (LEGACY KERNEL): the repo ships an ENTIRE ~4.1.10 kernel tree you must build and boot; it is not forward-ported to 5.x/6.x and the CSI hook is not upstream. Current reproducible CSI is via PicoScenes (QCA9300) on Ubuntu 22.04. Hardware (AR9580 etc.) remains cheap and plentiful. See ../docs/verification-tier2-csi.md and ../chips/qualcomm-atheros.md.

'Hornet' single-chip router SoC (MIPS 24Kc + integrated 1×1 2.4 GHz AR9003-class radio) driven by ath9k over the AHB bus. Spectral scan (Tier 3) + CSI via Atheros-CSI-Tool, monitor + injection. Ubiquitous in cheap OpenWrt routers.

The most widespread 'Hornet' SoC (TL-WR703N, MR3020, Onion Omega, Black Swift). ath9k/AHB SoftMAC with the AR9003 baseband: spectral scan (Tier 3) + CSI, monitor + injection. A $5 hackable spectrum-analyzer/CSI node.
'Wasp' 2×2 2.4 GHz router SoC, ath9k/AHB. AR9003 baseband: spectral scan (Tier 3) + CSI, monitor + injection.
'Wasp' dual-band 2×2 router SoC, ath9k/AHB. AR9003 baseband: spectral scan (Tier 3, both 2.4 and 5 GHz) + CSI, monitor + injection.

2x2 802.11n router SoC validated by the Atheros-CSI-Tool authors via the OpenWRT build path; yields per-packet CSI (Tier 2) and mainline ath9k spectral scan (Tier 3). Runs the modified ath9k on-device under OpenWRT — attractive for standalone/battery CSI sensing nodes rather than a host PC.

firmware.arch: none — SoftMAC (ar9003 baseband), driven by host ath9k driver

notes: AR9380 = 3x3, AR9382 = 2x2, AR9390 = integrated variant. Marketed as QCA9300 post-acquisition. CYCLE-7 SPOT-CHECK CORRECTION: removed `raw-iq` from sdr_capabilities. Primary sources (Atheros-CSI-Tool, ath9k) expose per-subcarrier CSI (complex H) and spectral-scan FFT magnitude bins only — neither is raw baseband I/Q, which would be a tier-4 capability this SoftMAC does not reach. raw-IQ was PicoScenes-reported flexibility, not a stock ath9k feature; it remains discussed here but is no longer asserted as a verified capability. Verified caps: monitor, injection, CSI, spectral scan (tier 3).

common_hardware: 2×2 dual-band 11n mini-PCIe (QCA9300 family, sibling of AR9380)
notes: AR9003 2×2 dual-band member of the QCA9300 family (the 2-stream cut of the AR9380). ath9k SoftMAC: spectral scan (Tier 3) + CSI. Covered by PicoScenes' QCA9300 receiver with arbitrary carrier tuning and 2.5-80 MHz baseband sampling.

sdr_reason: Low-cost 1x1 2.4GHz ar9003 part; still exposes spectral FFT (Tier 3) and single-stream CSI (Tier 2) through the open driver.

firmware.arch: none — SoftMAC (ar9003 baseband), driven by host ath9k driver

sdr_reason: 3x3 dual-band ar9003 desktop/router PCIe part; one of the explicitly tested Atheros-CSI-Tool targets. 3-stream CSI (Tier 2) and spectral FFT (Tier 3), no firmware mod.
notes: Atheros-CSI-Tool was validated on AR9580, AR9590, AR9344, QCA9558. Three RX chains give the richest CSI in the 11n line.

3x3 802.11n PCIe PHY explicitly validated by the Atheros-CSI-Tool authors for per-packet CSI extraction; also exposes the mainline ath9k spectral-scan debugfs interface (Tier 3, 56/128-bin FFT). No firmware patch needed — the driver drives the PHY directly. Sibling to AR9380/AR9580.

ANNOTATION/DOWNGRADE (merge on id): client-class ath10k. Spectral is firmware-image-dependent and often NOT exposed on QCA6174 mobile firmware, unlike AP chips (QCA988x/9984/9888). Do not claim clean Tier 3 without on-device confirmation; treated here as Tier 2/partial. AP-class QCA988x/QCA9984/QCA9888 remain verified Tier 3 and are unchanged.

Wilocity 'Sparrow' 60 GHz 802.11ad chipset: QCA6320 MAC/baseband + QCA6310 RF, driven by the mainline wil6210 driver with FullMAC firmware on ARC cores. SEEMOO's nexmon-arc patches wil6210 fw v4.1.0.55 / v5.2.0.18 to expose a 'sweep_dump' debugfs table of per-sector-sweep signal strength (beam-SNR). Beam-SNR is magnitude-only beam-space power, not per-subcarrier CSI, so we flag 'radar'/monitor/injection but deliberately NOT 'csi'. Tier 2: exports a spatial channel-state measurement usable as an angle-resolved pseudo-radar.

3x3 802.11n SoC explicitly validated by the Atheros-CSI-Tool authors (OpenWRT path); delivers 3x3 per-packet CSI (Tier 2) and ath9k spectral scan (Tier 3) with no firmware patch. On-device modified ath9k makes it a self-contained CSI sensing router.

firmware.arch: Tensilica Xtensa (on-chip), closed firmware blob loaded by ath10k

sdr_reason: 802.11ac wave-1. ath10k exposes the baseband spectral-scan FFT (spectral_bins 64/128/256) via debugfs — Tier 3. But the closed Xtensa firmware blocks the CSI path and constrains injection, so it sits below the ath9k parts despite newer silicon.
notes: Moving to 11ac introduced a closed on-chip firmware (unlike SoftMAC ath9k). ath10k-ct is a patched binary firmware, not open source. CSI is not turnkey on ath10k.

firmware.arch: Tensilica Xtensa (on-chip), closed firmware blob loaded by ath10k

sdr_reason: 802.11ac wave-2 (up to 4x4 MU-MIMO). Same Tier-3 spectral-scan FFT path as QCA988x; QCA9984/QCA9888 needed a kernel fix to strip an 8-byte segment-index header from each sample. Closed firmware, no turnkey CSI.
notes: 80+80/160 MHz support means wider FFT captures. QCA9888 is the 2x2 sibling.

802.11ac 4x4 Wi-Fi SoC, the pre-QSR10G Quantenna generation (now ON Semiconductor). Closed firmware with some GPL driver fragments in OpenWrt trees. CSI research exists on the newer catalogued qsr10g, not here. Tier 1.

firmware.arch: embedded Linux on quad ARC core cluster

notes: Runs embedded Linux internally on ARC cores; Quantenna publicly marketed Wi-Fi Sensing/CSI on these parts, making a documented CSI path plausible (tier 2 reported). No packaged community toolchain.

firmware.arch: Quantenna on-chip processor + MAC/PHY, closed firmware
re_tooling: vendor driver only; no packaged community tooling

common_hardware: QSR3610 client modules / retail Wi-Fi adapters
notes: Lower-tier 802.11ac client sibling of the catalogued quantenna-qsr10g. Quantenna marketed Wi-Fi Sensing/CSI at the platform level (see qsr10g), which makes a CSI path plausible here too, but there is no packaged public client tooling — so this is Tier 1 (monitor via vendor driver) with sensing status reported. Details are thin; part-number specifics are reported, not verified. Net-new record.

Small 802.11n + BT4.2 combo for appliance/metering hosts. DIE UNCONFIRMED (small Realtek-Ameba-class combo believed). Tier 1 IF the die is a Realtek rtw/rtl8xxx part -> cross-ref ../chips/realtek.md. Verify from FCC internal photos before relying on monitor support.

Open GPL mac80211 driver -> monitor + injection + sniffer in 902-928 MHz S1G channels. NO public CSI on any HaLow chip; PHY firmware is a closed blob. Honest Tier 1. Reported: confirm Newracom (vs Morse) die from FCC filing.

Integrator: standard Atheros/QCA 802.11 a/b/g/n/ac radios wrapped in the closed InstaMesh protocol. The dies could do monitor/injection under ath9k/ath10k, but the shipped firmware exposes only the mesh stack → practically Tier 1. Score by die.

Earliest Ralink generation, 802.11b 1T1R. Open rt2400pci SoftMAC driver gives monitor + injection (Tier 1) but the part is 2.4 GHz b-only and effectively obsolete. No CSI/spectral path ever existed for it.

common_hardware: Ralink RT2860/RT2760 MiniPCI/MiniPCIe internal Wi-Fi cards
notes: Net-new retro part; the first-generation 802.11n PCI/MiniPCIe Ralink MAC (rt2800pci sub-driver, shared rt2800lib core), i.e. the internal-card counterpart to the already-cataloged RT2870 USB parts in ../../chips/mediatek-ralink.md. SoftMAC monitor+injection via mac80211 = Tier 1; closed MAC microcode (rt2860.bin), no CSI/spectral. Same rt2800pci die family also spans RT3090/RT3390/RT5390 internal cards.
Low-cost 1T1R 802.11n mini-PCIe parts (RT3090, the RT3390 Wi-Fi/BT-combo variant, RT3060). Normal rt2800pci SoftMAC monitor + injection, Tier 1. Closed microcode; no PHY-telemetry path.
1T1R 802.11n + Bluetooth combo common in HP laptops. The Wi-Fi side is ordinary rt2800pci (Tier 1 monitor/injection, if sometimes finicky on Linux); Bluetooth is a separate function. No CSI/spectral.

MIPS router SoCs with integrated 2T2R (RT3352/RT3350) or 1–2 stream (RT305x) 802.11n radio, driven by the in-SoC rt2800soc path. Open SoftMAC → monitor + injection on OpenWrt (Tier 1). Closed MAC microcode; no CSI/spectral.

Very low-cost 1T1R 802.11n MIPS SoC (per OpenWrt, software-compatible with MT7620 but slower and without hardware 802.11w). rt2800soc SoftMAC → Tier 1 monitor/injection. Closed microcode; no PHY telemetry.

Late Ralink low-power 802.11n PCIe: RT5390 1T1R, RT5392 2T2R. Both rt2800pci SoftMAC → Tier 1 monitor/injection. The 2.4 GHz-only PCIe complement to the catalogued RT5370/RT5372 USB parts. Closed microcode; no CSI/spectral.

firmware.arch: proprietary Ralink/MediaTek on-chip MAC microcode (rt2870-series blob)

common_hardware: ASUS USB-N53 and dual-band USB n dongles
notes: Net-new retro part; the dual-band 2T2R 802.11n USB die driven by rt2800usb — the 5 GHz-capable 2T2R cousin of the already-cataloged RT5370/RT5372 (2.4-only) in ../../chips/mediatek-ralink.md, and a later, lower-power alternative to RT3572 for dual-band monitor/injection. SoftMAC, Tier 1; closed MAC microcode, no CSI/spectral. Good, widely-used injection with aircrack-ng.

firmware.arch: proprietary Ralink on-chip MAC microcode (rt2561.bin / rt2661.bin blobs)

common_hardware: many mid-2000s desktop and laptop internal cards
notes: Net-new retro part; the 802.11g PCI/MiniPCI sibling of the RT73 USB die, driven by rt61pci (rt2x00 family). SoftMAC, monitor+injection via mac80211 = Tier 1; small closed MAC microcode (rt2561.bin/rt2661.bin) from linux-firmware, no CSI/spectral. Cross-reference the modern MediaTek line and cataloged Ralink USB parts in ../../chips/mediatek-ralink.md.

The Ralink 802.11g generation (the 'RT2600'-class label in the sweep maps here): RT2561/RT2661 on rt61pci, RT2571W/RT2573 on rt73usb. Open SoftMAC drivers → reliable monitor + injection, a classic aircrack-ng-era g adapter. Tier 1 only; no CSI/spectral.

firmware.arch: proprietary Ralink on-chip MAC microcode (rt73.bin blob)

notes: Net-new retro part; not duplicated from ../../chips/mediatek-ralink.md (which covers RT2500/RT2570/RT2870/RT3070/RT3572/RT5370). SoftMAC 802.11b/g USB die driven by in-tree rt73usb (mac80211) and, historically, the out-of-tree serialmonkey 'rt73' driver plus ASPj injection mods (rausb0 interface, 'iwpriv rausb0 rfmontx 1'). Monitor+injection = Tier 1; on-chip MAC microcode (rt73.bin) is a small closed blob, no CSI/spectral. One of the earliest 'known-good injection' USB chipsets of the aircrack era. Same firmware/RE posture as the cataloged RT2870/RT3070 entries.

firmware.arch: Wi-Fi die = CYW43455 (Cortex-R4 + D11 ucode); BCM2711 AP has no radio

notes: SoC-level record. The BCM2711 application processor has NO radio; Wi-Fi is the on-board CYW43455 die — score and cross-reference broadcom-bcm43455c0. This is the reference Nexmon/nexmon_csi platform: monitor, injection and CSI @80MHz are verified on the Pi 4; the Tier-4 arbitrary-waveform/reactive-jamming capability is inherited from the die (WiSec'17, reported on Pi) and is TX — illegal on the air.

firmware.arch: Wi-Fi die = CYW43455 (same as Pi 4); BCM2712 AP has no radio

notes: SoC-level record. Carries the SAME CYW43455 die as the Pi 4 (broadcom-bcm43455c0), so the capability ceiling is identical (Tier 4). Marked reported, not verified, because the Pi 5 ships a newer 6.x kernel/brcmfmac and Nexmon builds for it are less battle-tested than the Pi 4 path. For friction-free CSI, prefer a Pi 4.

Realtek Ameba IoT line, the Realtek counterpart to Beken in Tuya modules. LibreTiny carries it (generic-rtl8710bn/bx board targets). Documented promiscuous/monitor mode (SmartConfig). Blob PHY; no verified CSI on this part (see AmebaD RTL8720DN for the CSI-capable sibling).

AmebaZ2 (Cortex-M4F). LibreTiny-supported (generic-rtl8720cf/cm targets). Documented promiscuous/monitor. Sibling of the already-catalogued RTL8720DN (AmebaD) which additionally exposes a documented CSI API; CSI on the Z2 part is plausible but unverified.
Realtek's original 802.11b PCI softMAC. Mainline rtl818x_pci is a mac80211 driver, so monitor + injection work out of the box. Historically important, band-limited (b only). Tier 1.
802.11g PCI successor to the 8180, same mainline rtl818x_pci softMAC path. Monitor + injection functional. Tier 1, 2.4 GHz only.

USB sibling of the famous 8187L, handled by the same mainline rtl8187 driver; monitor + injection supported. 802.11g, 2.4 GHz. Slightly different RF front-end than the 8187L (generally lower TX), but the same softMAC injection story. Tier 1.

firmware.arch: Thin on-chip MAC ucode (near soft-MAC to host)

notes: Original BackTrack-era injection card. Mainline mac80211 driver = monitor+injection out of the box. 2.4GHz only, high TX power. Tier 1.

1x1 802.11n USB variant of the RTL8192C family (8192CU already catalogued as the 2x2/generic part). 8188CUS is the Edimax EW-7811Un / classic Raspberry Pi dongle; 8188RU is the high-power radio used in the Alfa AWUS036NHR. Monitor + injection via rtl8xxxu / rtl8192cu. Tier 1.
PCIe 1x1 802.11n sibling of the 8188EU/EUS USB parts. rtlwifi rtl8188ee supports monitor RX; injection unreliable. Tier 1 (monitor only).
Cheap ubiquitous 2.4GHz n monitor/injection default. aircrack-ng/rtl8188eus is the reference DKMS driver. TL-WN722N v2/v3 use this (v1 was Atheros).
Later cheap 2.4GHz n part; monitor via out-of-tree forks, injection partial/flaky vs 8188EUS.
Newer low-cost 802.11n 1x1 USB part; recent rtl8xxxu adds support. Monitor works; injection reported but less battle-tested than 8188EUS. Tier 1.

PCIe 802.11n (8188CE = 1x1, 8192CE = 2x2). Mainline rtlwifi rtl8192ce registers monitor mode so RX capture works, but injection on rtlwifi is unreliable/broken. Tier 1 (monitor only) — not an injection card.
Very common 2.4GHz 802.11n dongle. Monitor works; injection quality depends on rtl8192cu vs rtl8xxxu driver.
Realtek's dual-band (2.4+5 GHz) 802.11n part — 8192DE (PCIe) and 8192DU (USB). Monitor RX via rtlwifi/rtl8192du; injection weak. Notable mainly as the first dual-band Realtek. Tier 1 (monitor only).
Early 802.11n PCIe (8191SE 1x1 / 8192SE 2x2), rtlwifi rtl8192se. Monitor RX works; injection unreliable. Tier 1 (monitor only).

Early Realtek 802.11n USB (RTL8712/8192SU). The in-tree r8712u staging driver is fullmac-ish and monitor support is limited/flaky; injection is not reliably supported. Catalogued for completeness. Tier 1 (monitor, partial).

The original Ameba Wi-Fi MCU (Cortex-M3, 802.11n). Open, documented FreeRTOS/Arduino SDK and promiscuous-mode ('monitor') APIs, but this generation predates the Wi-Fi CSI API — no per-subcarrier I/Q. Interesting as an open-firmware target, but honestly Tier 1 (no CSI). The RTL8711AM is the same Ameba1 die.

Older Realtek MIPS router SoCs with an integrated 2.4GHz 802.11n MAC. Realtek's driver stack is closed and mac80211 support is historically poor: monitor mode is limited and injection unreliable, capping around Tier 0-1 (reported). Not worth chasing when MediaTek exists. Distinct from the RTL838x/930x SWITCH SoCs, which have no radio at all.

NOT Wi-Fi chips: these are managed Ethernet switch ASICs with an embedded MIPS/embedded core. OpenWrt's realtek target supports them as switches. They contain no radio whatsoever — nothing to repurpose. Catalogued as N/A (Tier 0, empty capabilities) purely to prevent mis-identification as a latent radio.

Low-cost single-band Wi-Fi MCU (AmebaZ family), 2.4 GHz 802.11n, popular in cheap IoT (smart plugs/bulbs). Open documented SDK with promiscuous mode. Classic AmebaZ parts (8710AF/BN/BX) have no CSI API — Tier 1. Note: the newer RTL8710E belongs to the AmebaLite generation (separate record) and does expose CSI.

The SDR-interesting Realtek: dual-band Wi-Fi MCU with OFFICIAL Wi-Fi CSI API (per-subcarrier I/Q, amplitude+phase, active/passive modes). Open documented FreeRTOS SDK, Cortex-M4+M0. Cheap BW16 boards. Tier 2 / rung-2 CSI. Ameba CSI framework spans RTL8721Dx/8720E/8730E/8735C.

AmebaLite generation (RTL8720E/8710E/8713E/8726E). Realtek's Wi-Fi CSI docs explicitly list these as CSI-capable: per-subcarrier I/Q as S(8,4)/S(16,12) fixed-point with configurable subcarrier decimation, active or passive mode. Genuine rung-2 CSI on open/documented firmware. Tier 2, verified.

AmebaDplus successor to the catalogued RTL8720DN (RTL8721Dx / AmebaD). Listed in Realtek's CSI docs as CSI-capable (S(8,x)/S(16,x) I/Q). Dual-band + BLE, open documented SDK. Net-new rung-2 target alongside the 8720DN. Tier 2, verified.
2.4GHz n + Bluetooth combo. Station mode solid; monitor possible but injection weak/driver-dependent. Catalogued for completeness.
First-gen 1x1 802.11n + Bluetooth combo, PCIe. rtlwifi rtl8723ae monitor RX only; injection unreliable. Catalogued for completeness. Tier 1 (monitor only).
Extremely common 1x1 n+BT combo — 8723BE (PCIe) in countless budget laptops, 8723BS (SDIO) on tablets/SBCs. Monitor RX works; injection unreliable. Tier 1 (monitor only).
SDIO 1x1 n+BT combo common on TV boxes / SBCs, handled by rtw88 SDIO. Monitor RX; injection unsupported. Tier 1 (monitor only).
rtw88-era 1x1 n+BT combo across PCIe (8723DE), SDIO (8723DS), USB (8723DU). rtw88 registers monitor; injection is not a supported/reliable path. Tier 1 (monitor only).

AmebaSmart — a Linux-class Cortex-A55 SoC with dual-band ac Wi-Fi, listed in Realtek's CSI docs as CSI-capable. Higher compute makes it attractive for on-device Wi-Fi-sensing/CSI ML. Documented SDK. Tier 2, verified.

AmebaPro2 (RTL8735B/C) — Cortex-M33 AI-camera SoC with an on-chip NPU and dual-band ac Wi-Fi, listed in Realtek's CSI docs as CSI-capable. The NPU + CSI combination is uniquely suited to edge Wi-Fi-sensing (presence/gesture) without a host. Documented SDK. Tier 2, verified.

Common in low-cost wearables. DTM (CW/packet test) via vendor radio API repurposes it as a bare BLE PHY source; SDK largely closed and community RE thinner than Telink, so promiscuous sniffing is not a first-class documented mode.
1x1 dual-band AC sibling of 8812AU; same unified aircrack-ng driver. Monitor+injection. Tier 1.
Low-cost 1x1 ac USB part supported by out-of-tree rtl8811fu forks. Monitor usable; injection reported but fork-dependent. Tier 1.

PCIe 2x2 802.11ac — the card sibling of the ubiquitous 8812AU USB injection dongle. Mainline rtlwifi rtl8821ae drives it in monitor RX; injection is unreliable on rtlwifi (unlike the USB rtl8812au path). Tier 1 (monitor only).
THE standard dual-band 2x2 AC injection dongle. Alfa AWUS036ACH. aircrack-ng/rtl8812au is the reference driver. Tier 1, no CSI/spectral.
'B' gen 2x2 AC (8822BU = +BT combo). Monitor solid; injection partial/less reliable than 8812AU — morrownr steers pentesters back to 8812AU/8821CU.
rtw88 USB 2x2 ac part. Monitor works; injection possible but far less proven than the classic rtl8812au driver — treat injection as partial. Tier 1.

PCIe 4x4 802.11ac — card sibling of the AWUS1900's 8814AU. No solid mainline driver; out-of-tree rtl8814ae builds give station/monitor. Injection not a reliable path on the PCIe part. Tier 1 (monitor).
4x4 MIMO flagship (Alfa AWUS1900). Highest antenna count of Realtek line but still Tier 1. Dedicated rtl8814au fork adds AP+jammer; some distro rtl88xxau packages dropped 8814 support.
One of the most common 1x1 ac+BT combo cards in budget laptops. rtlwifi rtl8821ae supports monitor RX; injection unreliable. Tier 1 (monitor only).
1x1 AC (AU-series) covered by the unified aircrack-ng/rtl8812au driver. Monitor+injection. Tier 1.

Budget 1x1 ac+BT combo (PCIe/SDIO), mainline rtw88 rtw8821c. Monitor RX; injection unreliable. Tier 1 (monitor only). Distinct from the 8821CU USB dongle already catalogued (which does inject via morrownr's driver).
Single-stream dual-band AC; morrownr's recommended cheap/small injection adapter. Clean monitor+injection. Tier 1.
Mainstream 2x2 ac+BT combo, mainline rtw88 (rtw8822b). rtw88 supports monitor mode for capture; injection is not a supported/reliable path. PCIe (8822BE) + SDIO (8822BS). Tier 1 (monitor only).
Later revision of the 8822 2x2 ac+BT combo, extremely widely deployed. rtw88 rtw8822c monitor RX; injection unreliable. Tier 1 (monitor only).
USB variant of the 8822C combo. rtw88 USB / out-of-tree drivers give monitor; injection is partial and less reliable than 8812AU/8821CU. Tier 1.

Wi-Fi 6E 2x2 USB silicon (AXE3000-class dongles). Linux support is sparse/out-of-tree; monitor is unconfirmed on most builds and injection unproven. Catalogued as the 6 GHz USB frontier; verify per-dongle. Tier 1 aspirationally, currently monitor-theoretical.
Entry-level 1x1 Wi-Fi 6 + BT combo, rtw89 rtw8851b. Monitor RX supported by rtw89; injection unproven. Tier 1 (monitor only).
Realtek's first mass-market 2x2 Wi-Fi 6 + BT combo, the original rtw89 target. Mainline rtw89 supports monitor mode; injection is not a reliable path. Tier 1 (monitor only).

firmware.arch: Realtek WiFi 6 MAC, closed firmware; driven by rtw89

notes: CORRECTION (merge): injection removed, downgraded to monitor-only. Under mainline rtw89 monitor mode is experimental and injection is not dependable in 2025; unlike the older RTL8812AU/8821CU USB parts there is no mature out-of-tree injection driver to fall back on. Grade D.
The most widely deployed Realtek Wi-Fi 6 card, rtw89 rtw8852b. Monitor RX supported; injection unproven. Tier 1 (monitor only).

USB 2x2 Wi-Fi 6 part behind many AX1800 dongles. Driver support is early/out-of-tree; monitor is partial and injection unproven. Watch this one — a working injection driver would make it the first Realtek Wi-Fi 6 pentest USB. Tier 1 (monitor, partial).
Realtek's 2x2 Wi-Fi 6E part — adds the 6 GHz band. rtw89 rtw8852c monitor RX (incl. 6 GHz capture); injection unproven. Tier 1 (monitor only).

Realtek's first Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) client chip; the rtw89 repo explicitly names it as a Wi-Fi 7 device. Tri-band incl. 6 GHz, 320 MHz-capable. Mainline rtw89 supports monitor; injection unproven and no raw-PHY access. Tier 1 (monitor only) — the newest Realtek Wi-Fi silicon on the ladder.
Higher-end Realtek 10G managed switch SoC family. Like RTL838x, a switch ASIC with no radio. N/A for latent-radio work; listed for disambiguation.

RX-only 8-bit, ~0.5 kHz-1.7 GHz, ~2.4 MHz usable BW. The genuine-SDR floor and the accidental-SDR archetype; see rtl-sdr-lineage.md. Listed tier 5 as a reference datum only. Discovery: Eric Fry (2010) & Antti Palosaari (2012). CYCLE-7 SPOT-CHECK CORRECTION: bands ['sub-GHz','2.4GHz'] -> ['sub-GHz']. Primary source: RTL2832U + R820T/R820T2 tunes 24-1766 MHz (R828D tops out lower still); the dongle physically cannot tune the 2.4 GHz band, so the previous '2.4GHz' tag was ~600 MHz out of range. Upper ceiling ~1.766 GHz is L-band; mapped to 'sub-GHz' for lack of an L-band enum value.

802.11ah HaLow sub-GHz PHY/MAC IP from Dutch design house Methods2Business (acquired by Renesas, 2021). Sold as licensed IP/SoC; no public reversing path. The open HaLow route remains the catalogued Morse Micro parts. Tier 1, theoretical.
Tiny, cheap BLE SoC. prod_test firmware + DTM give CW/modulated TX and RX counting; register-level radio control via source-available SmartSnippets SDK enables proprietary 2.4 GHz experiments.

Cortex-M33 SmartBond with coprocessor-driven radio, higher TX power, ble_test/radio test path and an SDK radio API. DA1470x extends flash/graphics. Documented proprietary 2.4 GHz modes on the newer parts.

Ultra-low-power single-band (2.4 GHz) Wi-Fi 4 SoC with integrated Cortex-M4 and FreeRTOS SDK. Closed PHY; the SDK exposes a promiscuous/monitor RX path at best, with no documented CSI, injection, or raw-PHY access. Tier 1 (monitor plausible, injection/CSI unverified). Net-new Wi-Fi entry. Module vendors (Telit, Quectel, SparkLAN, Silex) are NOT distinct silicon - their SDR ceiling equals the underlying Realtek/Atheros/Cypress/Marvell die; identify via FCC-ID internal photos.

firmware.arch: integrated Wi-Fi SoC + separate BLE die; vendor FreeRTOS SDK only

notes: Ultra-low-power Wi-Fi IoT module (ex-Dialog, now Renesas): DA16200 Wi-Fi SoC paired with a DA14531 BLE die. Closed FreeRTOS SDK, no PHY/IQ access. Catalogued to complete the modern low-power IoT long-tail.

common_hardware: TBS Unify Pro and most analog FPV VTXes
notes: 5.8 GHz analog FM video transmitter IC: SPI-programmable carrier across 5645-5945 MHz, FM-modulates an ARBITRARY analog baseband input. Not IQ and single-modulation, but a genuine programmable-carrier transmitter of arbitrary baseband -> Tier 3 (arbitrary-waveform analog FM + covert-channel). SPI map is a first-class Betaflight driver. Companion RX5808 is a tunable 5.8 GHz FM downconverter with analog RSSI, occasionally used as a crude power sniffer.

common_hardware: Rockchip RK33xx/RK35xx SBCs and TV boxes
notes: Rockchip application SoCs ship no first-party WiFi silicon; their 'RTL-combo' boards pair an external Realtek (RTL8723DS/RTL8821CS/RTL8188FU) or AMPAK/Broadcom module over SDIO/USB. SDR capability is entirely that of the mounted die — chase the Realtek/Broadcom part, not the Rockchip label. Integration note, not net-new silicon.

family: RK3399 SBCs (+ AMPAK AP6xxx SDIO module)

firmware.arch: AP6256 = Cypress CYW43456-class die on brcmfmac; RK3399 AP has no radio

notes: SoC-level record. Rockchip ships no Wi-Fi silicon; RK3399 boards pair an AMPAK AP6xxx module (integrator package — see other-vendors.md). AP6256 carries a Cypress CYW43456-class die and rides brcmfmac, so Nexmon is theoretically portable (cross-ref broadcom-bcm43455c0), but no turnkey RK3399 nexmon_csi exists. AP6398S carries a BCM4359 (broadcom-bcm4359). Tier 1 as-shipped. See rockchip-realtek-combo-pairing.

family: RK3588 / RK3588S SBCs (+ AP6275P / AIC8800 / RTL8852BE)

firmware.arch: AP6275P = Broadcom BCM43752 Wi-Fi 6 die (no public Nexmon); or AIC8800 / RTL8852BE; AP has no radio

notes: SoC-level record. RK3588 boards pair AP6275P (Broadcom BCM43752 Wi-Fi 6 — no public Nexmon port), the AIC8800 (AICSemi, vendor-driver only), or PCIe RTL8852BE (see realtek.md). No open monitor/CSI path on the on-board module today => Tier 0-1. For sensing, use a USB adapter with a known die instead. Cross-ref router-ap-socs.md and rockchip-realtek-combo-pairing.

firmware.arch: Samsung HRP-UWB IC with AoA; FiRa-certified; host access via Android UWB API / UCI, closed firmware

notes: Net-new. Samsung's own FiRa-certified UWB IC (AoA-capable) used in Galaxy phones and the SmartTag2. Exposed to apps via the Android UWB API over FiRa UCI; closed firmware with no CIR/channel access. Tier 0 black box for SDR purposes; details on any raw access not public -> status reported.

Samsung's in-house baseband (codename Shannon). SCAT supports Shannon diag via `-t sec`, yielding GSMTAP control-plane capture — Tier 1 measurement. Heavy target of baseband security research (over-the-air Shannon exploitation), but the firmware remains a closed signed image. No IQ, no PHY.

firmware.arch: ARM Cortex-R modem cores; signed firmware with MPU-protected regions

notes: NOT an SDR. SCAT '-t sec' decodes Shannon diagnostic messages to GSMTAP. shannonRE (Comsecuris, RECON 2016) and FirmWire (NDSS 2022) enable firmware RE/emulation/fuzzing — security research, not IQ access. Band enum approximated as sub-GHz.
RX-only 14-bit, 1kHz-2GHz, up to 10MHz BW. Serious-listener receive tier.

Cost-reduced SX1262: same command set and CW mode but LoRa SF5-SF11 only (no SF12) and reduced max bandwidth. Same Tier 1 register-level repurposing as SX126x; note missing SF12 when emulating long-range links.

Multi-band LoRa/(G)FSK transceiver covering sub-GHz (150-960 MHz), 2.4 GHz ISM, and an S-band segment (~1.9-2.1 GHz) for direct-to-satellite LEO IoT. Register interface fully documented but it is a fixed modem: programmable LoRa/LR-FHSS/FSK/OOK/CW only, no raw IQ, no CSI, no spectral scan. Tier 1 covert-channel/FSK-abuse ceiling. S-band TX is licensed to sat operators only.

Second-gen LoRa transceiver, command/opcode SPI, 150-960 MHz, +15/+22 dBm. Arbitrary carrier + (G)FSK/LoRa packets, continuous-preamble mode, and SetTxContinuousWave for a bare tone. RadioLib exposes transmitDirect/receiveDirect but the old DIO clk/data raw-bitstream path of SX127x is largely gone. No IQ/PHY access -> Tier 1. SX1268 is the 470 MHz China variant.

LoRa (chirp spread spectrum) plus full (G)FSK/OOK legacy mode. Continuous FSK/OOK mode streams an arbitrary bitstream (tones, jamming, replay); the LoRa engine gives CSS TX/RX directly. The LoRa PHY was reverse-engineered on real SDRs (gr-lora by Bastille/Matt Knight and by rpp0), a good example of using an SDR to crack a closed PHY these chips then speak natively. SX1280 is 2.4 GHz LoRa.

LoRa in the 2.4 GHz ISM band, plus FLRC and (G)FSK. Hardware round-trip time-of-flight RANGING engine (cooperative ToF distance, not radar) and BLE-PHY compatibility so it can emit/sniff raw BLE-shaped 1 Mbps GFSK frames. Tier 1 transceiver; ranging is its distinguishing hook -> cross-link ftm-rtt-ranging. SX1281 is the reduced-package variant.

Purpose-built LTE-M/NB-IoT modems (Monarch/Monarch 2 add GNSS; Calliope is Cat-1). Interface is a documented AT command set plus a proprietary licensee-only logging tool. Firmware closed. You get control + measurement AT responses (signal quality, cell info) — Tier 0, no diag-grade OTA capture, no IQ.

family: Cellular + LoRa vendor (no merchant Wi-Fi die)
notes: POINTER RECORD, not an SDR target. Sierra Wireless (acquired by Semtech 2023) ships cellular basebands (-> ../chips/cellular-basebands.md) and rebrands Qualcomm/Atheros Wi-Fi in gateways (-> ../chips/qualcomm-atheros.md). Semtech's own RF is LoRa sub-GHz (SX127x, already catalogued as semtech-sx127x in ../chips/other-vendors.md / ../chips/lora-subghz.md) -- a chirp transceiver, NOT a Wi-Fi part. No independent Wi-Fi die exists to score.
2.4 GHz 802.11n IoT Wi-Fi combo used alongside SigmaStar (ex-MStar) camera SoCs. Closed vendor driver; limited monitor at best. Tier 1.

Industry-first IEEE 802.11ah Wi-Fi module, built on Newracom NRC7292. Range up to ~1.5 km; EVK targets Raspberry Pi. Inherits NRC7292 open GPL mac80211 driver (tier-1 monitor+injection) and closed radio firmware. Net-new named module record.

Reported to carry an Atheros AR9382 (ath9k) die — an open SoftMAC with monitor, injection, per-packet CSI (Atheros CSI Tool) and hardware spectral_scan → Tier 3. Capability from the die; see ../chips/qualcomm-atheros.md. Verify exact die by FCC ID; some Silex SX-PCE parts instead carry QCA9377 (Tier 1).
Carries the Infineon AIROC CYW54591 die (same die as Murata Type 1YN). Closed AIROC FW → Tier 1. See ../chips/broadcom-cypress.md.

Pre-certified modules wrapping the catalogued silabs-efr32 die. RAILtest gives CW/tone TX, arbitrary-channel packet TX/RX, coarse energy scan, PER, and a configurable PHY (rate/deviation/sync word). FG/Flex members add sub-GHz.

firmware.arch: ARM Cortex-M4/M33 + radio driven by RAIL library

notes: RAIL (Radio Abstraction Interface Layer) exposes an arbitrary proprietary-PHY builder (custom modulation, symbol rate, framing), plus energy/RSSI scanning and TX tone/stream mode. Radio internals closed but RAIL documented (partially-documented). Tier 1 with a path to custom PHYs.

firmware.arch: Cortex-M33 wireless SoC; radio internals closed, exposed through the documented RAIL library
re_tooling: RAIL (Radio Abstraction Interface Layer) arbitrary-PHY builder

notes: Series-2 successor to the catalogued silabs-efr32 (Series 1). RAIL still exposes an arbitrary proprietary-PHY builder (custom modulation, symbol rate, framing) plus energy/RSSI scanning and TX tone/stream modes on both sub-GHz and 2.4 GHz — enough to author custom simple-modulation waveforms (Tier 1, reaching toward arbitrary-waveform). Radio core closed but RAIL documented. FG25 targets sub-GHz 802.15.4g. Net-new record.

firmware.arch: Redpine/Silabs multiprotocol MAC/PHY, closed firmware; host runs the open rsi mac80211 driver

notes: Redpine Signals multiprotocol (Wi-Fi 4 + BT5 + 802.15.4), acquired by Silicon Labs. The mainline rsi mac80211 driver supports a monitor/sniffer mode (Tier 1) and radiotap injection; firmware is a closed blob with no public CSI. Net-new record.

First-gen EZRadioPRO. Si4432: 240-930 MHz, (G)FSK/OOK, the chip inside ubiquitous cheap RF4432/RFM22B modules and many alarm/sensor links -> prime RX-forensics and replay target. Si4438: 425-525 MHz China ISM variant. Classic direct mode with data+clock GPIO for raw bitstream. Well documented flat register map (openness documented).

119-1050 MHz, (G)FSK, 4(G)FSK, (G)MSK, OOK, up to 1 Mbps, -126 dBm (Si4468). Direct mode (TX/RX bitstream over GPIO with data+clock) gives the arbitrary keyed-waveform / protocol-forging lever. Register access is delivered as firmware patch + WDS-generated config blobs rather than a fully open flat map -> openness partially-documented; community projects reverse the WDS output. Si4464 range is 119-960 MHz.

firmware.arch: Cortex-M4 application core + closed 'network wireless processor' (NWP) running Wi-Fi 6 + BLE; WiSeConnect SDK
re_tooling: none public — WiSeConnect socket/offload API only

notes: Silabs' Wi-Fi 6 + BLE SoC: an M4 app core plus a closed network wireless processor that owns the radio and stack. The WiSeConnect SDK exposes only offloaded connectivity/socket APIs — no public monitor, raw 802.11, or CSI. Tier 0 (nominally 0-1 if a debug/PER test mode is unlocked, but nothing packaged for sensing). Net-new record.

firmware.arch: closed, signed Wi-Fi firmware on the WF200 transceiver; host runs the wfx mac80211 driver

notes: Looks like a Tier-1 candidate (mainline wfx mac80211 driver, in-tree since 5.5) but is honestly Tier 0: wfx_add_interface() only accepts NL80211_IFTYPE_STATION/ADHOC/AP and returns -EOPNOTSUPP for NL80211_IFTYPE_MONITOR (verified in drivers/net/wireless/silabs/wfx/sta.c), and the firmware is signed and closed. No public monitor/raw/CSI path. Included as an accuracy correction to the 'softmac must equal Tier 1' assumption. Net-new record.

Not a repurposable Wi-Fi die: an FPGA-based MIMO-OFDM soft radio running Silvus' proprietary MN-MIMO waveform (not 802.11). Genuinely software-defined internally but fully sealed — no open PHY, SDK, or driver. Black box, Tier 0; listed only for completeness of the ruggedized-mesh landscape.

firmware.arch: n/a (RF front-end IC, no firmware; sampler USB glue firmware is separate)

common_hardware: SparkFun GN3S Sampler v2/v3 (USB GPS L1 IF capture dongle)
notes: GPS L1 (SE4110) and dual-band (SE4120 'Stereo') GNSS RF front-ends. SE4110 is the front-end inside the classic SparkFun GN3S Sampler, one of the original tools that streamed raw GPS L1 IF samples to a PC for offline software correlation. Same story as MAX2769: RX-only, quantized IF out, single/dual GNSS band, no TX. Tier 3 raw-PHY RX front-end. Marked reported (front-end widely documented; some exact SE4120 band details vary by variant).

Single-band GPS/GNSS L1 front-end outputting 2-bit sign/magnitude raw IF samples - the classic academic SDR-GPS front-end (SiGe GN3S sampler, Borre/Akos software receiver). Genuine raw IF, RECEIVE ONLY, single band and coarse quantization -> Tier 4 (below the multi-band MAX2771). L-band not in band enum.
Carries the MediaTek MT7921 die (Wi-Fi 6 2x2 + BT, mt76). Monitor/injection via mt76 → Tier 1. Capability from the die; see ../chips/mediatek-ralink.md.

firmware.arch: QCA ath10k (open driver, signed FW blob)

notes: Carries the Qualcomm QCA6174A die (2x2 11ac + BT, ath10k). Monitor/injection but no reliable commodity spectral/CSI on this mobile part → Tier 1. See ../chips/qualcomm-atheros.md.

Carries an Atheros AR9382 (ath9k) die → monitor + injection + per-packet CSI (Atheros CSI Tool) + hardware spectral_scan = Tier 3, the best commodity-module RF-sensing story in this file. Capability from the die; see ../chips/qualcomm-atheros.md.

firmware.arch: QCA ath10k (open driver, signed FW blob)

notes: Carries the Qualcomm QCA9880 die (3x3 11ac, ath10k) → monitor, injection and FFT spectral scan = Tier 3. Firmware is a signed blob but the driver is open. Capability from the die; see ../chips/qualcomm-atheros.md.

firmware.arch: carrier board wrapping MediaTek MT7915 (Wi-Fi 6) or Qualcomm QCA silicon

notes: Carrier-board module house, not a silicon vendor. SDR capability inherits entirely from the underlying MediaTek MT7915 or Qualcomm QCA die — resolve to the chip file (mediatek / qualcomm-atheros) for the true tier.

BlueNRG-1/2/LP expose a documented low-level radio HAL for raw 2.4 GHz packet TX/RX (frequency, whitening, CRC, sync word, scheduled actions) plus DTM — genuinely injection-friendly despite a closed BLE stack. BlueNRG-MS is a network coprocessor (HCI/SPI only), effectively Tier 0/1.

firmware.arch: dual-core ARM Cortex-M4 + M0+ CPU2 (WB) or single M33 (WBA)

notes: CPU2 wireless coprocessor is a signed closed binary — no direct radio reprogramming. Raw hooks are limited to stack DTM (HCI) and OpenThread RCP/energy-scan. Least reverse-and-expose of the BLE group.

SX126x-class radio fused with an open Cortex-M4 (WLE5) or M4+M0+ (WL55) on one die; radio driven via internal SUBGHZSPI and fully register-documented in RM0453/RM0461. The one part here flagged open-firmware: no vendor blob between you and the modem, you write all firmware on open GCC. 150-960 MHz, LoRa/(G)FSK/(G)MSK/BPSK, +22 dBm. Most hackable for custom-PHY/timing/CTC work; still Tier 1 (no IQ/editable PHY).

VHF store-and-forward satellite-IoT modem (downlink ~137 MHz, uplink ~148 MHz). Closed MCU + proprietary transceiver behind a UART AT-style API; type-approved for the Swarm constellation only. No RF/IQ access. Tier 0. Transmitting on the VHF uplink outside the network is unlawful.

Integrator: Spectrum24 High-Rate cards carry an Intersil Prism2 die → classic monitor + injection via hostap. Capability is entirely the Prism2 die's; cross-reference the Prism2/2.5 family and chips/monitor-injection-support.md.

The most openly hacked non-Nordic BLE family: register-level RADIO, vendor source SDK, and a large community (pvvx) shipping fully custom open firmware with OTA. Multiprotocol BLE + 802.15.4 + Zigbee + proprietary; register-controlled GFSK enables custom links and raw sniffing.

firmware.arch: module rebrand of Redpine/Silicon Labs RS9113 single-die abgn+BT

notes: Module-vendor rebrand of the Redpine Signals (later Silicon Labs) RS9113 die; no independent silicon. Shipping firmware exposes no SDR path. Resolve to the RS9113 for true capability.
Die reported as a Realtek RTL8723-class 11n + BT combo. Tier 1 via the Realtek monitor path (cross-ref ../chips/realtek.md) IF confirmed. WE866C6 adds dual-band. Verify die from FCC grant.

Sealed 'network-processor' style Wi-Fi module. DIE UNCONFIRMED: candidates are a Redpine/Silabs RS9116-class (would be Tier 1 via open rsi driver) or a Qualcomm QCA401x IoT network processor (sealed Tier 0). Scored conservatively Tier 0-1 pending die confirmation. Cross-ref ../chips/other-vendors.md (RS9116 row).

firmware.arch: closed firmware blob uploaded at init; open reverse-engineered driver

notes: Fully open reverse-engineered driver around an opaque uploaded firmware blob — an early template for the 'open driver, closed firmware' split. ACX111 added 802.11g. Monitor works; injection partial.

firmware.arch: Cortex-R4F control + BIST; no user DSP

notes: 3TX/4RX 76-81 GHz FMCW transceiver used for cascade/imaging radar. Raw ADC streamed over LVDS to DCA1000. No on-chip user DSP - pure front-end. Tier 4 for radar only; TX is a chirp generator, not arbitrary IQ.
Single-chip 76-81 GHz FMCW radar, 3TX/4RX, Cortex-R4F plus a hardware accelerator for range/Doppler FFT. Raw ADC capture via mmWave Studio + DCA1000. Tier 4 radar only.
76-81 GHz FMCW radar, 2TX/4RX, with an on-die C674x DSP for on-chip range/Doppler processing. Both processed detections and raw ADC (via DCA1000) are available. Tier 4 radar.

firmware.arch: Cortex-R4F + C674x DSP + radar hardware accelerator

notes: Flagship 1st-gen single-chip 76-81 GHz FMCW radar: 3TX/4RX, C674x DSP plus a dedicated radar hardware accelerator. Full raw radar cube via DCA1000. AOP variant has antenna-on-package. Tier 4 radar.

2nd-gen 76-81 GHz FMCW transceiver (TX/RX only) built for cascade imaging radar - four devices give 12TX x 16RX = 192 virtual channels on MMWCAS. Raw ADC captured via DCA1000/DSP-EVM. Tier 4 imaging radar.

firmware.arch: Cortex-R5F + C66x DSP + radar HWA (2nd gen)

notes: Current-gen automotive single-chip 76-81 GHz FMCW radar, 4TX/4RX MIMO, C66x DSP + hardware accelerator, driven by mmWave Studio-2G. AWR2544 is the satellite/Ethernet single-chip sibling. Raw ADC via DCA1000. Tier 4 radar.

firmware.arch: register-configured transceiver (no CPU/firmware); SPI register set + async/sync serial data modes

notes: Narrowband OOK/ASK, 2-FSK/GFSK/4-FSK/MSK transceiver across 300-348, 387-464, 779-928 MHz. Not a true SDR: no raw IQ, fixed front-end, one channel at a time. Async serial mode carries the raw OOK envelope, enabling faithful capture/replay of arbitrary edge sequences (the arbitrary-waveform flag) but only at baseband-envelope level. Register/PATABLE fully documented in TI SWRS061.

137-950 MHz across six sub-bands, 2/4-(G)FSK, MSK, OOK/ASK, up to 1.25 Mbps, -123 dBm. Supports asynchronous and synchronous serial (transparent) modes on GPIO -> genuine direct bitstream path for arbitrary OOK/FSK waveform play and raw capture, same lever as CC1101. Targets 802.15.4g SUN-FSK and wM-Bus. CC1125 is the ultra-narrowband (12.5 kHz) variant; CC1120/CC1121 are lower-cost cuts. Register map documented (SWRU346).

Multiprotocol SimpleLink part covering both sub-GHz (ISM) and 2.4 GHz (BLE/Zigbee/Thread/802.15.4) with an on-chip Cortex-M0 radio core driven by a Cortex-M4F. Powers the open-hardware CatSniffer v3; with SmartRF/CatSniffer sniffer firmware it does multiprotocol packet capture into Wireshark (tier 1). Registers documented in the TRM; radio ROM closed. One dongle sees ISM remotes and Zigbee/BLE.

firmware.arch: Cortex-M3/M4 app core + dedicated Cortex-M0 RF Core with patchable ROM (RF patches)

notes: Two-core: Cortex-M3/M4 app + dedicated Cortex-M0 RF Core running the radio from a patchable ROM (RF patches). RF Core proprietary mode allows custom sub-GHz/2.4 GHz PHYs (arbitrary FSK/OOK params, packet formats); RSSI/CCA gives coarse spectrum sensing, reaching toward tier 3. driverlib open, RF ROM closed but patchable.

firmware.arch: transceiver (no MCU) paired with NXP LPC175x on Ubertooth

notes: Special case: CC2400 exposes an unbuffered demodulated bitstream plus a fast RSSI/energy sweep across the band. Ubertooth One uses this for BT BR/EDR + BLE sniffing and 2.4 GHz spectrum analysis (ubertooth-specan). Closest a commodity 2.4 GHz chip gets to SDR-lite; earns Tier 3.

First-gen Zigbee SoC: CC2420-class O-QPSK/DSSS PHY + 8051; CC2431 adds an RSSI location engine. Register-level RF control and unmodulated-carrier/PN9 test modes. Sniffing usually done with newer CC2531 dongle.
2.4 GHz sibling of CC1101 (GFSK/OOK/MSK) with the same transparent-mode raw-bitstream replay trick. The radio in many 2.4 GHz RC and peripheral links. Tier 1, documented PHY.

The catalogued CC2500 modem plus an 8051. SmartRF Studio exposes CW and PN9 modulated test TX and full register editing; packet engine can be disabled for near-raw framing. Sub-GHz siblings CC1110/CC1111 share the architecture.

CC2531 = 802.15.4/Zigbee USB sniffer; CC2540 = BLE sniffer. Stock sniffer firmware from TI, plus community whsniff+Wireshark (CC2531) and ZBOSS zboss_sniffer.hex. Tier 1 monitor within their standards; injection with custom firmware.
Low-power sibling of the catalogued CC2540 (adds I2C, drops USB). DTM and community observer/promiscuous firmwares give raw advertising-channel capture. Ubiquitous in HM-10 modules.

firmware.arch: ARM Cortex-M4 app core + closed network processor

notes: TI's own silicon (CC3220S) in a certified can. The 802.11 MAC/PHY runs on a closed on-module network processor exposing only a sockets/TLS API -- no host mac80211, no monitor iftype, no raw path. This is the 'SimpleLink = anti-SDR' family (CC3000->CC3235 row) in ../chips/other-vendors.md. Tier 0, verified.

firmware.arch: ARM Cortex-M4 (80MHz) app core + closed Wi-Fi network processor

notes: Dual-band (2.4/5 GHz) SimpleLink module around the CC3235S die. Same sealed network-processor architecture as CC3220 -> Tier 0. Verified from TI product page. MODASF variant adds 1MB XIP flash. Cross-ref ../chips/other-vendors.md.

Purpose-built radar included as a tier-4 yardstick, NOT a repurposed Wi-Fi chip. Single-chip FMCW radar: IWR6843 at 60-64 GHz; AWR1642/AWR6843 at 76-81 GHz (automotive, band outside this catalog's enum). Full control of the FMCW chirp (start freq/slope/ramp) and raw ADC IQ streamed off-chip via DCA1000EVM -> range/Doppler/angle FFT. Tier 4 justified natively by raw-iq. CORRECTION (cycle-8 audit batch 2): removed arbitrary-waveform — the TX path is a fractional-N chirp generator (programmable FMCW ramps), not baseband-IQ authoring; consistent with sibling ti-awr1243, whose note states 'TX is a chirp generator, not arbitrary IQ.'

family: SimpleLink Wi-Fi CC3000 / CC3100 / CC3200 / CC3220 / CC3230 / CC3235 (closed network processor)

firmware.arch: closed ROM-based 'network processor' (own MCU) alongside optional Cortex-M4 app core (CC32xx); Wi-Fi + full IP stack sealed inside
re_tooling: none public — only the SimpleLink host driver / socket API

notes: The anti-SDR. The radio, MAC, and entire TCP/IP + TLS stack live inside a closed ROM 'network processor' that the host reaches only through a BSD-socket / networking API (HTTPS/mDNS/DHCP/TLS). No monitor mode, no raw 802.11, no PHY telemetry is exposed; CC3235 adds 2.4/5 GHz dual-band but the sealing is identical. Genuinely Tier 0 with no public RE path short of attacking the NWP. Catalogued to mark the floor of the ladder. Net-new record.

firmware.arch: WiLink 8 die + closed FW blob; open wlcore mac80211 driver; Sitara AP has no radio

notes: SoC-level record. Sitara APs carry no radio; Wi-Fi is the WiLink 8 module (WL1835/WL1837MOD) — cross-ref ti-wl18xx (older Sitara used WL12xx, ti-wl12xx). The open wlcore mac80211 driver gives standard `iw ... type monitor`, so monitor is verified. Firmware blob is closed; no CSI/spectral path => Tier 1.

firmware.arch: WiLink MAC/PHY, closed firmware blob (ti-connectivity/wl127x-fw in linux-firmware)

notes: Older WiLink 6/7 sibling of the catalogued ti-wl18xx. WL1271 is 2.4 GHz only; WL128x add 5 GHz. Fully open mac80211 driver (wl12xx + wlcore) gives monitor + radiotap injection out of the box (Tier 1); firmware is a closed blob from linux-firmware/ti-connectivity with no CSI/PHY path. Net-new record.

Open mac80211 driver stack (wlcore+wl18xx+wlcore_sdio) gives monitor mode and radiotap injection. Firmware is a closed blob from git.ti.com; no CSI/PHY-telemetry path and no public patching toolchain, so the ladder stops at tier 1.

firmware.arch: Synopsys ARC (ARCompact) WiGig firmware; MIPS/ARM host running LEDE/OpenWrt

notes: The workhorse of practically all 60 GHz Wi-Fi sensing research: 32-element planar phased array, single 60 GHz stream. Teardowns show Sparrow QCA6320+QCA6310 silicon; sensing papers commonly write 'QCA9500 transceiver' for the same wil6210/ARC family. SEEMOO's LEDE port gives root + custom firmware loading; nexmon-arc's sweep_dump exposes per-sector beam-SNR at /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phyX/wil6210/sweep_dump. Used for device-free localization, gesture recognition, and short-range SAR imaging via aperture motion. Distinct from the already-cataloged qualcomm-qca9500 chip record.

Integrator only: TYWE* modules are ESP8266 (→ chips/espressif.md, monitor/injection/CSI), WB2/WB3/WBR are Beken BK7231N/T or Realtek RTL8720 (→ chips/realtek.md). SDR ceiling = the die's; the ESP8266 variants reach the listed tier, Beken/RTL variants are lower/closed. No new capability of its own.

Die = Cypress/Broadcom CYW89359 (Wi-Fi 5 2x2 + BT5). Score at the die's tier — see ../chips/broadcom-cypress.md. brcmfmac gives monitor/injection; CYW89359 is Nexmon-adjacent but has no confirmed Nexmon port, so no CSI/spectral credited. Honest Tier 1.
Die = NXP 88W8987 (Marvell Avastar family). Tier of the die per ../chips/other-vendors.md — mwifiex/moal netlink monitor + injection, no public CSI. Score = Tier 1.
Die = NXP 88W9098 (Wi-Fi 6 2x2 + BT5.2). Maps to the '88W9098' row in ../chips/other-vendors.md — NXP moal/mlan monitor+injection, no CSI path. Tier 1.

Die = NXP IW612 single-chip tri-radio (Wi-Fi6 + BT5 + 802.15.4). See the 'IW611/IW612' row in ../chips/other-vendors.md. Tier 1 (monitor/injection via moal), no CSI. Reported: verify exact part from FCC grant.

Low-power 802.11n + BT host-based module. DIE UNCONFIRMED from public docs (believed a Marvell/NXP SD8801-class 1x1 11n part). Scored Tier 1 provisionally; confirm the die from the FCC internal photos before relying on it. Cross-ref ../chips/other-vendors.md.

firmware.arch: closed u-blox GNSS baseband; public UBX interface description

notes: Single-band but raw-capable u-blox modules (timing M8T / precision M8P) exposing UBX-RXM-RAWX carrier-phase + RXM-SFRBX raw nav bits, ~$40-75 -> the affordable entry to raw carrier phase and RTKLIB-based RTK/PPP. Tier 2 (measurement/phase layer). RX-only correlator, no IQ, no TX, firmware closed.

Die = Espressif ESP32. Inherits the documented ESP-IDF CSI API (per-subcarrier I/Q via esp_wifi_set_csi) -> Tier 2, the standout u-blox Wi-Fi module. Cross-ref ../chips/espressif.md. Same package philosophy as JODY but a much higher tier purely because of the die.
Die = Espressif ESP32-S3. Same ESP-IDF CSI path as NORA-W10 -> Tier 2. Cross-ref ../chips/espressif.md.

Stand-alone dual-band Wi-Fi + BT module. Die reported as a Qualcomm QCA4004-class Wi-Fi + CSR BT combo; radio is sealed behind u-blox firmware, so effectively Tier 0-1 with no exposed host 802.11 stack. Cross-ref ../chips/qualcomm-atheros.md. Verify die from FCC grant.

firmware.arch: third-party baseband (varies by series) behind u-blox firmware

notes: SARA modules wrap third-party baseband behind u-blox firmware and a well-documented AT interface (+ m-center diagnostics). SARA-R5 adds GNSS. Firmware closed; access is measurement + control AT only. Tier 0 for SDR purposes — no OTA frame capture, no IQ.

firmware.arch: closed u-blox GNSS baseband; public UBX interface description

notes: Dual-band RTK receiver that outputs RAW observables via UBX-RXM-RAWX: pseudorange, CARRIER PHASE (cycles), Doppler, C/N0 per satellite, plus raw nav bits (RXM-SFRBX). Onboard RTK reaches ~cm accuracy (0.01 m + 1 ppm) with corrections. Carrier phase is a genuine per-satellite phase observable (the GNSS analogue of Wi-Fi CSI) -> Tier 2. NOT IQ, NOT transmit-capable, firmware closed. Honest price note: bare modules ~$150-220 on breakout boards, not $30. RTKLIB is the standard open toolchain that turns RXM-RAWX into RTK/PPP positioning.

79 GHz 4D imaging 'radar-on-chip' using digital code modulation (PMCW/DCM) - phase-coded spread-spectrum rather than FMCW ramps, hence an arbitrary-waveform-adjacent flag. Up to ~192 virtual channels, on-chip correlation. Uhnder wound down operations in 2024, so tooling is effectively orphaned. Tier 4 radar.
Cortex-M4 2.4GHz 11n WiFi SoC (RDA, absorbed into Unisoc), notable for an Arm Mbed OS port that documents the RTOS/driver layer. WiFi PHY remains a blob; monitor via driver. Tier 1.

Low-cost WiFi+BT combo. GPL sprdwl_ng kernel driver (AOSP vendor trees, not mainline) provides standard nl80211 monitor mode; on-chip firmware is a downloaded closed blob so SDR ceiling is plain monitor. UWE5621 = 2.4GHz 11n, UWE5622 adds 5GHz 11ac.

Carries a Broadcom BCM4330 die (dual-band 11n + BT). Monitor/injection only → Tier 1. USI (Universal Scientific Industrial) modules span Broadcom/Cypress/Qualcomm/NXP dies depending on the customer SKU — always confirm the die by FCC ID. See ../chips/broadcom-cypress.md.

Low-cost ARM Cortex-M3 2.4GHz Wi-Fi SoC (the 'domestic ESP8266'). The WM SDK and community Arduino/MicroPython ports are open (open-firmware), but the PHY/baseband is a closed blob with no published monitor/CSI/injection interface — Tier 0. Carried inside various Tuya/Lierda/Ai-Thinker modules.

Cortex-M3 Wi-Fi 802.11 b/g/n + BLE combo, W60x successor. Open SDK/toolchain (open-firmware) but closed PHY — no monitor/CSI/spectral path, so Tier 0. Popular as a cheap ESP32 alternative in Chinese IoT modules.

firmware.arch: USB softMAC; MAC in host via mac80211

notes: Open softMAC USB part (ZyDAS acquired by Atheros in 2006). Clean monitor+injection made ZD1211 dongles a long-running aircrack-ng recommendation. ZD1201 was the older 802.11b-only sibling.
